beats.say: A $5 razor that never stops costing.
Buy the razor alone, no blades.
Buy the razor with a bundle of blades.
Buy the razor, blades, and a premium case for the same price.
First year sold 51 razors and 168 blades. Looks mismatched.
But the cheap razor is a loss-leader; blades generate profit.
In the second year razor sales jumped to 90,884, while blade sales kept rising.
Each new razor forces a fresh blade purchase, the only recurring revenue.
Customers pay $5 once, then keep buying disposable blades.
Barbershop offers a cheap clipper handle, then pricey replaceable blades.
Coffee shop sells a $2 reusable cup, then $0.30 per refill.
Now the refill feels smart because the handle cost is sunk.
Notice the one-time buy and the repeat-buy trap. Follow for more.
